headline: DPM METALS PRINTS RECORD $227M FREE CASH FLOW IN Q2 — Vareš AISC $563/GEO, Ramp-Up On Track; Brevene South Porphyry Copper-Gold Discovery At Chelopech (TSX: DPM)
snippet: DPM Metals (TSX: DPM, ASX: DPM) — the company formerly known as Dundee Precious Metals — reported record quarterly free cash flow of $227 million in Q2 2026, published July 30, with revenue surging 94% year-over-year to $362 million and adjusted net earnings more than doubling to $211 million ($0.95 per share). The result was driven by elevated gold prices and the continued ramp-up of the Vareš silver-zinc-lead mine in Bosnia and Herzegovina — acquired via the 2025 Adriatic Metals combination — which processed 117,000 tonnes in Q2 at an AISC of $563 per gold-equivalent ounce, one of the lowest cost structures in the mid-tier gold sector globally. DPM ended the quarter with $761 million in cash, zero debt, and a $400 million undrawn credit facility — making it one of the strongest balance sheets relative to market capitalisation in the Canadian mid-tier gold space. A critical forward-looking catalyst accompanies the earnings: in June 2026, DPM confirmed the discovery of high-grade copper-gold porphyry mineralisation at the Brevene South Porphyry (BSP) target at the Chelopech mine in Bulgaria, with initial drill results demonstrating scale and continuity potential that the company describes as transformational. For investors tracking the gold equity re-rating thesis, DPM's Q2 result is one of the strongest FCF-per-share stories in the Canadian mining sector — and at the current share price, the company is generating free cash flow at a rate that represents an extraordinary return on capital relative to peers. The BSP discovery optionality adds a district-scale exploration dimension to an already strong cash-generating base.

headline: CAMECO Q2: URANIUM REALIZED PRICE CLIMBS 15% TO $93.13/LB — Revenue Guidance Raised To $3.32-3.57B; EBITDA $391M; Stock +4.3% On Apparent 'Earnings Miss' (NYSE: CCJ, TSX: CCO)
snippet: Cameco Corp. (NYSE: CCJ, TSX: CCO) reported Q2 2026 results that initially appeared to miss Street estimates — adjusted EBITDA of $391 million, net earnings of $25 million, and adjusted EPS of $0.127 versus the $0.28 consensus — but the stock rose 4.3% in pre-market trading when investors parsed what was actually happening: the realized uranium price in the segment climbed 15% to $93.13 per pound, production remained fully on track at 10.1 million pounds year-to-date within the 19.5–21.5 million pound annual guidance, and management raised full-year consolidated revenue guidance to $3.32–$3.57 billion (uranium segment $2.70–$2.91B) with a uranium realized price target of $91–$96 per pound for the full year. Operational disruptions — spring road conditions affecting Key Lake and McArthur River supply routes, and a ~two-week Cigar Lake suspension for operational reasons — temporarily reduced volumes and elevated unit costs, but management confirmed these events do not affect the full-year production outlook. For junior uranium investors, the most important data point from the Cameco result is the $91–$96 per pound long-term contract price range: that is the price floor at which the world's largest pure-play uranium producer is currently signing utility supply contracts. With spot uranium at $86.60 per pound and rising 21% year-on-year, the spread between spot and long-term is narrowing — a historical precursor to spot price acceleration.

headline: ENDEAVOUR SILVER Q2: REVENUE +150% TO $212M, NET EARNINGS $66.5M — Terronera Ramp Drives 31% Silver Growth; AISC $36.89/oz At $57-59/oz Spot (NYSE: EXK, TSX: EDR)
snippet: Endeavour Silver Corp. (NYSE: EXK, TSX: EDR), a mid-tier Mexican silver producer, reported Q2 2026 results on July 29 showing revenue surging 150% year-over-year to $212.1 million and net earnings of $66.5 million — driven primarily by the ramp-up of the Terronera underground mine in Jalisco, Mexico, which reached commercial production in October 2025 and is progressively accessing higher-grade silver zones. Q2 silver production rose 31% to 1.94 million ounces; gold production grew 35% to 10,474 ounces, combining for 3.4 million silver-equivalent ounces. Mine operating cash flow jumped 300% to $99.9 million before taxes. Consolidated AISC was $36.89 per ounce of silver — an exceptionally competitive cost structure for a primary silver producer at a moment when spot silver is trading at $57–$59/oz, implying gross operating margins above $20 per ounce. Cash on hand reached $236 million with working capital of $214 million. The LNG plant at Terronera commenced commissioning in June and is now operating, reducing energy costs into H2 2026. Terronera is expected to access higher-grade silver zones in H2 2026, which management projects will lower unit costs further. For investors tracking primary silver producers, Endeavour's Q2 result is the best combination of grade, volume growth, and margin expansion in the primary silver sector this quarter — and with $236 million in cash and a credible path to lower AISC into year-end, it enters H2 2026 in the strongest financial position since Terronera's development began.

headline: COPPER $6.43/LB AS LME INVENTORY DROPS 10,000 TONNES IN ONE SESSION — China Import Premiums Hit 2022 High; Codelco Chairman: "No Possibility" of 1.7M Tonne Target Within 5 Years
snippet: Copper's two-track structural story — near-term inventory tightening and long-term supply structural deficit — converged dramatically around August 1, 2026: London Metal Exchange copper warehouse stocks fell by more than 10,000 tonnes in a single session to 262,300 tonnes, while Chinese import premiums reached their highest level since 2022, signalling physical scarcity of refined copper in the world's largest consuming market. Spot copper sat at $6.43 per pound (approximately $14,180 per tonne), up 14% year-to-date, and nearby LME contracts traded at a premium (backwardation) to forward months — the physical market's signal of near-term supply inadequacy. The structural backdrop deepened this week: Codelco's new chairman Bernardo Fontaine stated there is 'no possibility' of the company reaching its stated 1.7 million tonne annual output target within five years, with 2026 guidance capped at approximately 1.357 million tonnes — 21–23% below Codelco's 2015 output peak. The world's largest copper producer, responsible for approximately a quarter of global mined supply, has now definitively acknowledged that its declining ore grades, aging mine infrastructure, and capital programme challenges cannot be overcome within the horizon that copper demand forecasts project accelerating supply gaps. For junior copper developer investors on the TSX-V and ASX, Codelco's acknowledgement crystallises the supply-side case: if the company with the world's largest copper resource base cannot reverse its own production decline, new supply must come from projects currently in development — and that supply is needed before 2030.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD DISCOVERS TWO NEW DEEP GOLD STRUCTURES AT GOLD ROCK, ONTARIO — Elora 2 Confirmed At 250-500m Depth; Mud Lake Permit Secured With 93 g/t Surface Samples (TSXV: DRY)
snippet: Dryden Gold Corp. (TSXV: DRY, OTCQX: DRYGF) announced July 29–30, 2026 that its 2026 drill program at the Gold Rock Gold Project in Dryden, northwestern Ontario has confirmed the discovery of two new gold-bearing structures that significantly expand the system's known footprint. The new Elora 2 structure was intersected at 250 to 500 metres true depth in a zone between the Elora and Big Master gold systems — with mineralisation characterised as brecciated quartz veining comparable to the Big Master system, yet lacking any surface expression, indicating it is a blind structure discoverable only through systematic deep drilling. A second new structure was confirmed at the historic Paymaster target. The discoveries arrive as Dryden Gold simultaneously received a drill permit for the Mud Lake target — a high-grade shear zone with surface samples returning 93.00 g/t gold in channel samples, representing an entirely separate discovery corridor that management has flagged as a priority for the next drill phase beginning mid-August. Dryden Gold is executing a CA$17.5 million, approximately 45,000-metre drill program in 2026 — one of the most aggressive exploration budgets for a TSXV-listed junior. For retail investors tracking Ontario gold exploration, the Elora 2 discovery is significant for one specific reason: blind structures confirmed at 250-500 metres depth within an established mineralized system indicate the gold system is vertically extensive well below what surface expressions would suggest, expanding the resource inventory potential dramatically.

headline: BOLD VENTURES BURCHELL REE FOOTPRINT GROWS — Up To 3,060 ppm TREO Found 3.2km From Discovery Hole In Hermia Pluton; 29% Are Magnet REEs (TSXV: BOL)
snippet: Bold Ventures Inc. (TSXV: BOL) announced on July 30, 2026 that its 2026 exploration program at the Burchell Project — located 100 kilometres west of Thunder Bay in Ontario's Western Shebandowan Greenstone Belt — has identified widespread rare earth element anomalies in grab samples and drill core from the Hermia pluton, located 2.2 to 3.2 kilometres east of the company's initial March 2026 REE discovery drill hole BL-26-05A. Surface samples from multiple outcrops in the Hermia pluton returned anomalous grades exceeding 500 ppm Total Rare Earth Oxides (TREO), with a peak of 3,060 ppm TREO (0.3%) — confirming that REE mineralisation is not isolated to the original discovery zone but appears distributed across a significantly larger geological footprint. The initial discovery hole BL-26-05A returned a 55.2-metre interval averaging 1,022 ppm TREO within syenite intruded by carbonate veining, with 29% of the Total REOs comprising the Magnet Rare Earth Oxides (MREOs) — neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium — the elements essential to permanent magnets used in EV motors, wind turbines, and defence hardware. For investors tracking Ontario REE exploration, the Hermia pluton anomalies increase the odds that Burchell hosts a district-scale REE system rather than a single isolated occurrence. The 2.2–3.2 km separation between the anomalies and the discovery hole implies a structural corridor controlling REE emplacement — the same style of geometry seen in large magmatic and hydrothermal REE deposits — and justifies the Phase 3 program Bold is now planning.

headline: BMO: CHINA'S GOLD COULD OVERTAKE US RESERVES IN LESS THAN FIVE YEARS — PBoC Bought 570 Tonnes Covertly In 2024; RMB Strategy Needs 2,500-3,000 More Tonnes (GoldSeek)
snippet: BMO Capital Markets analysts and Money Metals' researcher Mike Maharrey have independently reached the same conclusion: China's People's Bank of China gold accumulation program is on track to surpass US gold reserves of 8,133 tonnes within two to five years, depending on the actual pace of covert buying. China officially reports 2,346 tonnes of gold reserves — sixth globally — but independent research by analyst Jan Nieuwenhuijs estimates the PBoC covertly acquired 570 tonnes of additional gold in 2024 alone, routing purchases through state-owned entities and the Shanghai Gold Exchange in a manner that escapes official reporting. If the official pace continues — 7 tonnes added per month officially in Q1 2026 — parity with the US in official terms would take approximately 20 years. But at the covert pace estimated by Nieuwenhuijs, the actual PBoC holding already likely exceeds 4,000 tonnes, with parity achievable within five years if buying continues. The strategic rationale is explicit: China's ambition to internationalise the renminbi and reduce dollar dependency in trade settlement requires credible gold backing — a goal that financial analysts estimate requires holdings of 10,000–12,000 tonnes. For investors in gold mining equities, the China accumulation thesis provides the most structurally reliable demand floor under gold prices: sovereign gold buying is inelastic to price, tends to accelerate on dips, and is explicitly policy-driven rather than speculative.

headline: 5 GOLD STOCKS FOR H2 2026: ANALYSTS CITE 40% DISCOUNT TO HIGHS, RECORD FCF AS 'GENERATIONAL' BUY — Agnico, Kinross, Alamos Among Top Picks
snippet: Canadian Mining Report has published an H2 2026 gold equity positioning piece citing a rare setup that occurs when gold is trading at historically elevated prices ($4,000+/oz) while gold mining stocks remain 30–40% below their 2026 highs. The analysis focuses on five gold producers — including Agnico Eagle, Kinross Gold, and Alamos Gold — that are generating record free cash flow at current gold prices while trading at implied long-term gold price assumptions of $3,200–$3,800 per ounce as reflected in their equity valuations. The disconnect between what physical gold trades at and what gold equities imply in their NAV discounts represents what institutional analysts are characterising as a 'generational entry point' — a term historically applied when producer stocks lag metals prices before a re-rating cycle. The report notes that both Anglogold Ashanti and Agnico Eagle have fallen approximately 40% from their 2026 highs despite the underlying gold price remaining above $4,000, which means investors can effectively buy the same ounces of gold production at 60 cents on the dollar versus what the gold price alone would imply. For retail investors in junior mining, the stock valuation divergence between seniors and spot gold is directly relevant: if seniors re-rate toward NAV at spot gold assumptions, the valuation multiple expansion in TSX-V and ASX junior developers — which trade at even steeper NAV discounts — would be disproportionately large.

headline: MINING M&A H1 2026: BMO LEADS AS GOLD AND COPPER CONSOLIDATION HITS $21.6B — Strongest Start Since 2023; Deal Count Halved While Value Surged 63%
snippet: Global mining mergers and acquisitions reached $21.6 billion in H1 2026 — the strongest first-half value since 2023 and up 63% from H1 2025 — with BMO Capital Markets ranking as the top financial adviser for mining M&A by deal value, according to sector league tables published in July 2026. The structural pattern is notable: deal count fell sharply (roughly halved from H1 2025 levels) while total deal value surged, indicating a market dominated by fewer but much larger transactions — megadeals in gold and copper rather than a broad wave of small-company consolidation. Gold-sector M&A accounted for approximately $7.9 billion across four major 2026 transactions including the Equinox Gold-Orla Mining combination, with copper-focused deals driven by the Glencore-Rio Tinto merger discussions — now legally permitted to resume in August after the UK Takeover Panel's six-month cooling-off period expired. The concentration of deal value in gold and copper reflects which commodities offer the most compelling M&A rationale at current prices: gold's record FCF margins create currency for acquirers, while copper's structural supply deficit justifies paying premium multiples for development assets in advance of a production gap that most analysts project will materialize in 2027–2028. For retail investors in junior mining stocks on the TSX-V and ASX, the H1 M&A data validates the thesis that the sector's best assets are attracting institutional and strategic capital at a rate not seen since the 2010–2012 M&A super-cycle.

headline: URANIUM SPOT $86.60/LB, UP 21% YEAR-ON-YEAR — Utilities Locking Long-Term At $91-96/Lb; Peninsula Energy Withdraws 2026 Guidance; Paladin Drills New Body At Patterson Lake South (INN)
snippet: Uranium's Q2 2026 market review reveals a commodity consolidating at structurally elevated prices after the surge to $101/lb in January: spot uranium settled at $86.60/lb as of July 31, 2026 — up 21.2% year-on-year — in a market where term contract prices from utility buyers are running $91–$96/lb (per Cameco's Q2 guidance disclosure), confirming that the long-term procurement market is stronger than the spot market. The sustained elevated price environment is generating divergent company-level outcomes: Cameco achieved a 15% increase in average realized uranium price to $93.13/lb in Q2 while maintaining full-year production guidance despite temporary Cigar Lake disruptions. In contrast, Peninsula Energy (ASX: PEN) withdrew its 2026 production guidance for the Lance Uranium Project in Wyoming, citing operational development challenges — though the company reconfirmed 2027 guidance of 500,000–600,000 pounds U3O8. On the exploration side, Paladin Energy completed its 2026 winter drilling programme at Patterson Lake South in Saskatchewan, with the company reporting the discovery of a new uranium body — an addition to the Athabasca Basin inventory that underscores the active new discovery phase in the world's highest-grade uranium district. For investors tracking the uranium cycle, the Q2 data portrait is one of structural demand outpacing supply at $86+ per pound: utilities are signing long-term contracts at $91–$96/lb, producers who can deliver are generating record margins, and new supply developments in both ISR operations and the Athabasca Basin are advancing on schedule for 2027+ production.
